sanskrit: atra niḥśreyasaṃ yan nas tad dhyāyasva pitāmaha tvatprabhāvasamuttho 'sau prabhāvo no vinaśyati
english: Ponder for us, O Grandsire, what here is our highest good; that power of ours which sprang from your power is now perishing.

sanskrit: tān uvāca surān sarvān svayaṃbhūr bhagavāṃs tataḥ śreyo 'haṃ cintayiṣyāmi vyetu vo bhīḥ surarṣabhāḥ
english: Then the blessed Self-Born spoke to all those gods: I shall devise what is best; let your fear depart, O bulls among the gods.

sanskrit: tato 'dhyāyasahasrāṇāṃ śataṃ cakre svabuddhijam yatra dharmas tathaivārthaḥ kāmaś caivānuvarṇitaḥ
english: Then, born of his own mind, he composed a hundred thousand chapters, wherein dharma, and likewise artha, and kāma too were set forth.

sanskrit: trivarga iti vikhyāto gaṇa eṣa svayaṃbhuvā caturtho mokṣa ity eva pṛthagarthaḥ pṛthaggaṇaḥ
english: This group, proclaimed by the Self-Born as the trivarga, the threefold aim; and the fourth, namely mokṣa, a distinct aim and a distinct group of its own.

sanskrit: mokṣasyāpi trivargo 'nyaḥ proktaḥ sattvaṃ rajas tamaḥ sthānaṃ vṛddhiḥ kṣayaś caiva trivargaś caiva daṇḍajaḥ
english: And for mokṣa too another triad was declared: sattva, rajas, and tamas; while stability, increase, and decline are the triad that springs from the rod of rule.

sanskrit: ātmā deśaś ca kālaś cāpy upāyāḥ kṛtyam eva ca sahāyāḥ kāraṇaṃ caiva ṣaḍvargo nītijaḥ smṛtaḥ
english: The self, the place, and the time, the means, the deed to be done, the allies, and the cause as well: this is remembered as the sixfold set born of statecraft.

sanskrit: trayī cānvīkṣikī caiva vārtā ca bharatarṣabha daṇḍanītiś ca vipulā vidyās tatra nidarśitāḥ
english: The triple Veda, and philosophic inquiry, and economy, O bull of the Bharatas, and the broad science of statecraft: these branches of knowledge are there shown forth.

sanskrit: amātyarakṣāpraṇidhī rājaputrasya rakṣaṇam cāraś ca vividhopāyaḥ praṇidhiś ca pṛthagvidhaḥ
english: The safeguarding and surveillance of ministers, the guarding of the king's son, espionage by manifold means, and surveillance of various kinds.

sanskrit: sāma copapradānaṃ ca bhedo daṇḍaś ca pāṇḍava upekṣā pañcamī cātra kārtsnyena samudāhṛtā
english: Conciliation, and the giving of gifts, division, and punishment, O Pāṇḍava, and a fifth, indifference: these too are here set forth in full.

sanskrit: mantraś ca varṇitaḥ kṛtsnas tathā bhedārtha eva ca vibhraṃśaś caiva mantrasya siddhyasiddhyoś ca yat phalam
english: Counsel too is described entire, and likewise the matter of sowing dissension, and the failure of counsel, and the fruit that lies in its success or failure.

sanskrit: saṃdhiś ca vividhābhikhyo hīno madhyas tathottamaḥ bhayasatkāravittākhyaḥ kārtsnyena parivarṇitaḥ
english: And treaty of manifold name, the inferior, the middling, and the superior, that called of fear, of honor, and of wealth, is described in full.

sanskrit: yātrākālāś ca catvāras trivargasya ca vistaraḥ vijayo dharmayuktaś ca tathārthavijayaś ca ha
english: And the four seasons for a campaign, and the elaboration of the threefold aim; conquest joined with righteousness, and likewise conquest for gain.

sanskrit: āsuraś caiva vijayas tathā kārtsnyena varṇitaḥ lakṣaṇaṃ pañcavargasya trividhaṃ cātra varṇitam
english: And the demonic conquest too is thus described in full; and the threefold character of the fivefold set is here set forth.

sanskrit: prakāśaś cāprakāśaś ca daṇḍo 'tha pariśabditaḥ prakāśo 'ṣṭavidhas tatra guhyas tu bahuvistaraḥ
english: The open and the hidden form of force is then declared: the open is there of eight kinds, while the covert is of vast extent.

sanskrit: rathā nāgā hayāś caiva pādātāś caiva pāṇḍava viṣṭir nāvaś carāś caiva deśikāḥ pathi cāṣṭakam
english: Chariots, elephants, horses, and foot soldiers too, O Pāṇḍava, levied labor, boats, spies, and guides upon the road: these are the eight.

sanskrit: aṅgāny etāni kauravya prakāśāni balasya tu jaṅgamājaṅgamāś coktāś cūrṇayogā viṣādayaḥ
english: These, O Kaurava, are the open limbs of an army; and the mobile and immobile applications of powders, poisons, and the like are also told.

sanskrit: sparśe cābhyavahārye cāpy upāṃśur vividhaḥ smṛtaḥ arir mitram udāsīna ity ete 'py anuvarṇitāḥ
english: In what is touched and in what is eaten, secret poisoning of many kinds is recorded; the foe, the friend, and the neutral, these too are described.

sanskrit: kṛtsnā mārgaguṇāś caiva tathā bhūmiguṇāś ca ha ātmarakṣaṇam āśvāsaḥ spaśānāṃ cānvavekṣaṇam
english: The full merits of routes, and likewise the merits of terrain, self-protection, the heartening of troops, and the oversight of spies.

sanskrit: kalpanā vividhāś cāpi nṛnāgarathavājinām vyūhāś ca vividhābhikhyā vicitraṃ yuddhakauśalam
english: The manifold marshalings of men, elephants, chariots, and horses, battle arrays of various name, and the wondrous skill of warfare.

sanskrit: utpātāś ca nipātāś ca suyuddhaṃ supalāyanam śastrāṇāṃ pāyanajñānaṃ tathaiva bharatarṣabha
english: Portents and downfalls, the well-fought fight and the well-managed retreat, and the lore of tempering weapons, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: balavyasanamuktaṃ ca tathaiva balaharṣaṇam pīḍanāskandakālaś ca bhayakālaś ca pāṇḍava
english: The disasters of an army are set forth, and likewise the rousing of an army to joy; the time for harrying and assault, and the time of peril, O Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: tathā khātavidhānaṃ ca yogasaṃcāra eva ca caurāṭavyabalaiś cograiḥ pararāṣṭrasya pīḍanam
english: And the contrivance of trenches, and the deployment of stratagems, and the harassing of a hostile realm by fierce bands of robbers and forest folk.

sanskrit: agnidair garadaiś caiva pratirūpakacārakaiḥ śreṇimukhyopajāpena vīrudhaś chedanena ca
english: By arsonists and poisoners, by spies in disguise, by suborning the heads of guilds, and by the cutting down of crops.

sanskrit: dūṣaṇena ca nāgānām āśaṅkājananena ca ārodhanena bhaktasya pathaś copārjanena ca
english: By the corrupting of elephants, by the breeding of mistrust, by cutting off provisions, and by seizing the roads.

sanskrit: saptāṅgasya ca rājyasya hrāsavṛddhisamañjasam dūtasāmarthyayogaś ca rāṣṭrasya ca vivardhanam
english: The fitting decline and growth of the kingdom with its seven limbs, the right employment of an envoy's powers, and the increase of the realm.

sanskrit: arimadhyasthamitrāṇāṃ samyak coktaṃ prapañcanam avamardaḥ pratīghātas tathaiva ca balīyasām
english: The handling of foe, neutral, and friend is rightly told; and the crushing and the repulse of those who are stronger.

sanskrit: vyavahāraḥ susūkṣmaś ca tathā kaṇṭakaśodhanam śamo vyāyāmayogaś ca yogo dravyasya saṃcayaḥ
english: Most subtle litigation, and likewise the clearing away of thorns; peace, the exertion of effort, and the gathering and amassing of goods.

sanskrit: abhṛtānāṃ ca bharaṇaṃ bhṛtānāṃ cānvavekṣaṇam arthakāle pradānaṃ ca vyasaneṣv aprasaṅgitā
english: The maintenance of the unsupported, the care of dependents, giving at the proper time of need, and abstention from the vices.

sanskrit: tathā rājaguṇāś caiva senāpatiguṇāś ca ye kāraṇasya ca kartuś ca guṇadoṣās tathaiva ca
english: Likewise the virtues of a king, and those virtues that belong to a commander, and the merits and faults of the instrument and of the agent as well.

sanskrit: duṣṭeṅgitaṃ ca vividhaṃ vṛttiś caivānujīvinām śaṅkitatvaṃ ca sarvasya pramādasya ca varjanam
english: The manifold tokens of malice, and the conduct of dependents, wariness toward all, and the shunning of negligence.

sanskrit: alabdhalipsā labdhasya tathaiva ca vivardhanam pradānaṃ ca vivṛddhasya pātrebhyo vidhivat tathā
english: The desire to gain the ungained, and likewise the increase of what is gained, and the giving of what has grown to worthy recipients according to rule.

sanskrit: visargo 'rthasya dharmārtham arthārthaṃ kāmahetunā caturtho vyasanāghāte tathaivātrānuvarṇitaḥ
english: The disbursing of wealth for the sake of dharma, for the sake of gain, and for the sake of pleasure, and a fourth in the warding off of calamity: these too are here described.

sanskrit: krodhajāni tathogrāṇi kāmajāni tathaiva ca daśoktāni kuruśreṣṭha vyasanāny atra caiva ha
english: The fierce vices born of wrath, and likewise those born of desire, ten in all, O best of the Kurus, are here declared.

sanskrit: mṛgayākṣās tathā pānaṃ striyaś ca bharatarṣabha kāmajāny āhur ācāryāḥ proktānīha svayaṃbhuvā
english: Hunting, dicing, drink, and women, O bull of the Bharatas, the teachers call those born of desire, and they were here proclaimed by the Self-Born.

sanskrit: vākpāruṣyaṃ tathogratvaṃ daṇḍapāruṣyam eva ca ātmano nigrahas tyāgo 'thārthadūṣaṇam eva ca
english: Harshness of speech, and ferocity, and harshness in punishment, oppression of oneself, prodigality, and the squandering of wealth.

sanskrit: yantrāṇi vividhāny eva kriyās teṣāṃ ca varṇitāḥ avamardaḥ pratīghātaḥ ketanānāṃ ca bhañjanam
english: Engines of many kinds, and their workings, are described; the crushing assault, the repulse, and the shattering of standards.

sanskrit: caityadrumāṇām āmardo rodhaḥkarmāntanāśanam apaskaro 'tha gamanaṃ tathopāsyā ca varṇitā
english: The destruction of sacred trees, the breaking of sieges and the ruin of workshops, the removal of obstacles, the march, and the means of attendance are described.

sanskrit: paṇavānakaśaṅkhānāṃ bherīṇāṃ ca yudhāṃ vara upārjanaṃ ca dravyāṇāṃ paramarma ca tāni ṣaṭ
english: Of small drums, kettledrums, conches, and war drums, O best of warriors, the gathering of materials and the chief vital points: these are the six.

sanskrit: labdhasya ca praśamanaṃ satāṃ caiva hi pūjanam vidvadbhir ekībhāvaś ca prātarhomavidhijñatā
english: The settling of what is won, the honoring of the good, union of purpose with the learned, and knowledge of the rite of the morning oblation.

sanskrit: maṅgalālambhanaṃ caiva śarīrasya pratikriyā āhārayojanaṃ caiva nityam āstikyam eva ca
english: The touching of auspicious things, the care of the body, the ordering of food, and constant piety as well.

sanskrit: ekena ca yathottheyaṃ satyatvaṃ madhurā giraḥ utsavānāṃ samājānāṃ kriyāḥ ketanajās tathā
english: How a man should rise unaided, truthfulness, sweet words, the holding of festivals and assemblies, and the rites that arise on the raising of standards.

sanskrit: pratyakṣā ca parokṣā ca sarvādhikaraṇeṣu ca vṛttir bharataśārdūla nityaṃ caivānvavekṣaṇam
english: Conduct both open and concealed in all the offices of state, O tiger of the Bharatas, and constant vigilance.

sanskrit: adaṇḍyatvaṃ ca viprāṇāṃ yuktyā daṇḍanipātanam anujīvisvajātibhyo guṇeṣu parirakṣaṇam
english: The immunity of brāhmaṇas from punishment, the just infliction of punishment, and the safeguarding of merit on behalf of dependents and one's own kindred.

sanskrit: rakṣaṇaṃ caiva paurāṇāṃ svarāṣṭrasya vivardhanam maṇḍalasthā ca yā cintā rājan dvādaśarājikā
english: The protection of the townsfolk and the increase of one's own realm, and that deliberation upon the circle of states, O king, the doctrine of the twelve kings.

sanskrit: dvāsaptatimatiś caiva proktā yā ca svayaṃbhuvā deśajātikulānāṃ ca dharmāḥ samanuvarṇitāḥ
english: And the doctrine of the seventy-two, which was declared by the Self-Born, and the laws of regions, of castes, and of families are fully described.

sanskrit: dharmaś cārthaś ca kāmaś ca mokṣaś cātrānuvarṇitaḥ upāyaś cārthalipsā ca vividhā bhūridakṣiṇāḥ
english: Dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa are here described, and the means and the pursuit of wealth, manifold and with abundant sacrificial fees.

sanskrit: mūlakarmakriyā cātra māyā yogaś ca varṇitaḥ dūṣaṇaṃ srotasām atra varṇitaṃ ca sthirāmbhasām
english: The working of sorcery by roots, and illusion and magic, are here described, and the fouling of flowing streams and of still waters is set forth.

sanskrit: yair yair upāyair lokaś ca na caled āryavartmanaḥ tat sarvaṃ rājaśārdūla nītiśāstre 'nuvarṇitam
english: By whatsoever means the world might be kept from straying from the path of the noble, all that, O tiger among kings, is described in the science of statecraft.

sanskrit: etat kṛtvā śubhaṃ śāstraṃ tataḥ sa bhagavān prabhuḥ devān uvāca saṃhṛṣṭaḥ sarvāñ śakrapurogamān
english: Having wrought this auspicious treatise, the blessed Lord, well pleased, then spoke to all the gods led by Śakra.

sanskrit: upakārāya lokasya trivargasthāpanāya ca navanītaṃ sarasvatyā buddhir eṣā prabhāvitā
english: For the benefit of the world and for the establishing of the threefold aim, this wisdom, the very cream of eloquence, has been brought forth.

sanskrit: daṇḍena sahitā hy eṣā lokarakṣaṇakārikā nigrahānugraharatā lokān anu cariṣyati
english: For this, joined with the rod of chastisement, works the protection of the world, and, intent on restraint and on favor, it shall move among the worlds.

sanskrit: daṇḍena nīyate ceyaṃ daṇḍaṃ nayati cāpy uta daṇḍanītir iti proktā trīṃl lokān anuvartate
english: And this is guided by the rod, and it guides the rod in turn; therefore it is called daṇḍanīti, the rule of the rod, and it pervades the three worlds.

sanskrit: ṣāḍguṇyaguṇasāraiṣā sthāsyaty agre mahātmasu mahattvāt tasya daṇḍasya nītir vispaṣṭalakṣaṇā
english: Holding the essence of the six measures of policy, it shall stand foremost among the great-souled; and by the greatness of that rod, the rule has its clear mark.

sanskrit: nayacāraś ca vipulo yena sarvam idaṃ tatam āgamaś ca purāṇānāṃ maharṣīṇāṃ ca saṃbhavaḥ
english: And the broad course of policy, by which all this is spread abroad, and the lore of the ancient tales, and the origin of the great sages.

sanskrit: tīrthavaṃśaś ca vaṃśaś ca nakṣatrāṇāṃ yudhiṣṭhira sakalaṃ cāturāśramyaṃ cāturhotraṃ tathaiva ca
english: The succession of holy fords, and the lineage of the constellations, O Yudhiṣṭhira, the whole order of the four life stages, and likewise the rite of the four priests.

sanskrit: cāturvarṇyaṃ tathaivātra cāturvedyaṃ ca varṇitam itihāsopavedāś ca nyāyaḥ kṛtsnaś ca varṇitaḥ
english: The system of the four classes, and likewise the fourfold knowledge of the Vedas, is here described; the epic histories and the subsidiary Vedas, and the whole science of right reasoning, are set forth.

sanskrit: tapo jñānam ahiṃsā ca satyāsatye nayaḥ paraḥ vṛddhopasevā dānaṃ ca śaucam utthānam eva ca
english: Austerity, knowledge, and non-injury, truth and falsehood, the highest polity, attendance upon elders, giving, purity, and exertion as well.

sanskrit: sarvabhūtānukampā ca sarvam atropavarṇitam bhuvi vācogataṃ yac ca tac ca sarvaṃ samarpitam
english: And compassion for all beings, all this is here described; whatever upon the earth has passed into speech, all of it has been brought together.

sanskrit: tasmin paitāmahe śāstre pāṇḍavaitad asaṃśayam dharmārthakāmamokṣāś ca sakalā hy atra śabditāḥ
english: In that treatise of the Grandsire, O Pāṇḍava, this is beyond doubt: dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa are here all proclaimed entire.

sanskrit: tatas tāṃ bhagavān nītiṃ pūrvaṃ jagrāha śaṃkaraḥ bahurūpo viśālākṣaḥ śivaḥ sthāṇur umāpatiḥ
english: Then the blessed Śaṃkara first received that science of polity, he of many forms, the wide-eyed, Śiva, Sthāṇu, the lord of Umā.

sanskrit: yugānām āyuṣo hrāsaṃ vijñāya bhagavāñ śivaḥ saṃcikṣepa tataḥ śāstraṃ mahārthaṃ brahmaṇā kṛtam
english: Perceiving the dwindling of the ages and of the lifespan of men, the blessed Śiva then abridged the treatise of great import that Brahmā had made.

sanskrit: vaiśālākṣam iti proktaṃ tad indraḥ pratyapadyata daśādhyāyasahasrāṇi subrahmaṇyo mahātapāḥ
english: It was called the Vaiśālākṣa, after the wide-eyed one; that Indra received, the well-versed in sacred lore, of great austerity, in ten thousand chapters.

sanskrit: bhagavān api tac chāstraṃ saṃcikṣepa puraṃdaraḥ sahasraiḥ pañcabhis tāta yad uktaṃ bāhudantakam
english: The blessed Puraṃdara too abridged that treatise into five thousand chapters, my son, and it is called the Bāhudantaka.

sanskrit: adhyāyānāṃ sahasrais tu tribhir eva bṛhaspatiḥ saṃcikṣepeśvaro buddhyā bārhaspatyaṃ tad ucyate
english: But into three thousand chapters Bṛhaspati, the lord, abridged it by his wisdom, and it is called the Bārhaspatya.

sanskrit: adhyāyānāṃ sahasreṇa kāvyaḥ saṃkṣepam abravīt tac chāstram amitaprajño yogācāryo mahātapāḥ
english: Into a thousand chapters Kāvya declared the abridgment of that treatise, he of boundless wisdom, the master of yoga, of great austerity.

sanskrit: evaṃ lokānurodhena śāstram etan maharṣibhiḥ saṃkṣiptam āyur vijñāya martyānāṃ hrāsi pāṇḍava
english: Thus, out of regard for the world, this treatise was abridged by the great sages, perceiving the waning lifespan of mortals, O Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: atha devāḥ samāgamya viṣṇum ūcuḥ prajāpatim eko yo 'rhati martyebhyaḥ śraiṣṭhyaṃ taṃ vai samādiśa
english: Then the gods, assembling, said to Viṣṇu, the lord of creatures: Appoint that one who alone among mortals is worthy of supremacy.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃcintya bhagavān devo nārāyaṇaḥ prabhuḥ taijasaṃ vai virajasaṃ so 'sṛjan mānasaṃ sutam
english: Then, having reflected, the blessed god Nārāyaṇa, the lord, brought forth a mind-born son, full of splendor and free of passion.

sanskrit: virajās tu mahābhāga vibhutvaṃ bhuvi naicchata nyāsāyaivābhavad buddhiḥ praṇītā tasya pāṇḍava
english: But Virajas, O greatly fortunate one, desired no sovereignty upon the earth; his mind was bent solely upon renunciation, O Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: kīrtimāṃs tasya putro 'bhūt so 'pi pañcātigo 'bhavat kardamas tasya ca sutaḥ so 'py atapyan mahat tapaḥ
english: Kīrtimat was his son; he too passed beyond the five senses; and Kardama was his son, and he too performed great austerity.

sanskrit: prajāpateḥ kardamasya anaṅgo nāma vai sutaḥ prajānāṃ rakṣitā sādhur daṇḍanītiviśāradaḥ
english: Of Kardama the lord of creatures there was indeed a son named Anaṅga, a protector of the people, a good man, skilled in the science of statecraft.

sanskrit: anaṅgaputro 'tibalo nītimān adhigamya vai abhipede mahīrājyam athendriyavaśo 'bhavat
english: Anaṅga's son Atibala, versed in polity, having attained it, came to the kingship of the earth; but then he fell under the sway of his senses.

sanskrit: mṛtyos tu duhitā rājan sunīthā nāma mānasī prakhyātā triṣu lokeṣu yā sā venam ajījanat
english: Now the daughter of Death, O king, mind-born, named Sunīthā, renowned throughout the three worlds, gave birth to Vena.

sanskrit: taṃ prajāsu vidharmāṇaṃ rāgadveṣavaśānugam mantrapūtaiḥ kuśair jaghnur ṛṣayo brahmavādinaḥ
english: Him, lawless toward his subjects and a slave to passion and hatred, the sages who expound the sacred word struck down with blades of kuśa grass made potent by mantras.

sanskrit: mamanthur dakṣiṇaṃ corum ṛṣayas tasya mantrataḥ tato 'sya vikṛto jajñe hrasvāṅgaḥ puruṣo bhuvi
english: The sages, by force of mantra, churned his right thigh; thereupon there was born of him upon the earth a misshapen man of stunted limbs.

sanskrit: dagdhasthāṇupratīkāśo raktākṣaḥ kṛṣṇamūrdhajaḥ niṣīdety evam ūcus tam ṛṣayo brahmavādinaḥ
english: Like a charred stump to look upon, red-eyed and black-haired, to him the sages who expound the sacred word said, 'Sit down' (niṣīda).

sanskrit: tasmān niṣādāḥ saṃbhūtāḥ krūrāḥ śailavanāśrayāḥ ye cānye vindhyanilayā mlecchāḥ śatasahasraśaḥ
english: From him sprang the Niṣādas, cruel, dwelling in mountains and forests, and the others by hundreds of thousands, the barbarians abiding in the Vindhyas.

sanskrit: bhūyo 'sya dakṣiṇaṃ pāṇiṃ mamanthus te maharṣayaḥ tataḥ puruṣa utpanno rūpeṇendra ivāparaḥ
english: Again those great sages churned his right hand; thereupon a man arose, like a second Indra in his form.

sanskrit: kavacī baddhanistriṃśaḥ saśaraḥ saśarāsanaḥ vedavedāṅgavic caiva dhanurvede ca pāragaḥ
english: Clad in armor, his sword girded on, bearing arrows and bow, knowing the Vedas and their auxiliaries, and a master of the science of archery.

sanskrit: taṃ daṇḍanītiḥ sakalā śritā rājan narottamam tataḥ sa prāñjalir vainyo maharṣīṃs tān uvāca ha
english: In him, that best of men, the whole science of statecraft took its abode, O king; then the son of Vena, with hands joined in reverence, spoke to those great sages.
